42307-frank-in-the-woods.title: Frank In The Woods.
42307-frank-in-the-woods.creator: Harry Castlemon,
42307-frank-in-the-woods.description: A book by Harry Castlemon,. It was a cold, dreary night. The wind moaned and whistled through the leafless branches of the trees, sending the snow in fitful gusts through every nook and corner of the forest. On the banks of a small lake, that lay hemmed in on all sides by tall trees, which bowed to every gust of the winter's storm, was an encampment.

arxiv-1612-04509.title: Banach limits and traces on ℒ 1 , ∞ \mathcal{L}_{1,\infty} . Journal: Advances in Mathematics
arxiv-1612-04509.creator: Evgeniy Semenov, Fedor Sukochev, Alexandr Usachev, Dmitriy Zanin
arxiv-1612-04509.description: A 2016 arXiv research paper by Evgeniy Semenov, Fedor Sukochev, Alexandr Usachev, Dmitriy Zanin. We introduce a new approach to traces on the principal ideal ℒ 1 , ∞ \mathcal{L}_{1,\infty} generated by any positive compact operator whose singular value sequence is the harmonic sequence. Distinct from the well-known construction of J. Dixmier, the new approach provides the explicit construction of every trace of every operator in ℒ 1 , ∞ \mathcal{L}_{1,\infty} in terms of translation invariant functionals applied to a sequence of restricted sums of eigenvalues.

arxiv-2005-11805.title: Bayesian Multiresolution Modeling of Georeferenced Data
arxiv-2005-11805.creator: John Paige Department of Statistics, University of Washington,Geir-Arne FuglstadDepartment of Mathematical Sciences, NTNU,Andrea RieblerDepartment of Mathematical Sciences, NTNU, and Jon Wakefield Departments of Statistics and Biostatistics, University of Washington
arxiv-2005-11805.description: Abstract Current implementations of multiresolution methods are limited in terms of possible types of responses and approaches to inference. We provide a multiresolution approach for spatial analysis of non-Gaussian responses using latent Gaussian models and Bayesian inference via integrated nested Laplace approximation (INLA).

arxiv-2108-07266.title: The tree world
arxiv-2108-07266.creator: Markos Maniatis
arxiv-2108-07266.description: Abstract Tree amplitudes of any gauge theory and gravity can be factorized into primitive three-particle amplitudes by the BCFW recursion relations. We show that the amplitudes at any perturbation order are given by tree amplitudes with additional pairs of particles in the forward limit. As an example we compute the four-gluon all-plus helicity amplitude at next-to-leading order.

arxiv-2309-09546.title: Training early-exit architectures for automatic speech recognition: fine-tuning pre-trained models or training from scratch
arxiv-2309-09546.creator: George August Wright 1 , Umberto Cappellazzo 1 , Salah Zaiem 2 , Desh Raj 3 , Lucas Ondel Yang 4 , Daniele Falavigna 5 , Mohamed Nabih Ali 5 , Alessio Brutti 5
arxiv-2309-09546.description: Abstract The ability to dynamically adjust the computational load of neural models during inference is crucial for on-device processing scenarios characterised by limited and time-varying computational resources. A promising solution is presented by early-exit architectures, in which additional exit branches are appended to intermediate layers of the encoder.

arxiv-2311-06979.title: Assessing the Interpretability of Programmatic Policies with Large Language Models
arxiv-2311-06979.creator: Zahra Bashir, Michael Bowling, Levi H. S. Lelis
arxiv-2311-06979.description: Abstract Although the synthesis of programs encoding policies often carries the promise of interpretability, systematic evaluations were never performed to assess the interpretability of these policies, likely because of the complexity of such an evaluation. In this paper, we introduce a novel metric that uses large-language models (LLM) to assess the interpretability of programmatic policies.

arxiv-2407-19667.title: Smart Language Agents in Real-World Planning
arxiv-2407-19667.creator: Annabelle Miin, Timothy WeiPacific Collegiate School, Saratoga High School annabellemiin8@gmail.com, timswei@gmail.com
arxiv-2407-19667.description: Abstract Comprehensive planning agents have been a long term goal in the field of artificial intelligence. Recent innovations in Natural Language Processing have yielded success through the advent of Large Language Models (LLMs). We seek to improve the travel-planning capability of such LLMs by extending upon the work of the previous paper TravelPlanner (Xie et al., ( 1 ) ).

pmc-11286854.title: Determinants of melon farmers’ adaptation strategies to climate change hazards in south‒south Nigeria
pmc-11286854.creator: Adeyinka Richard Aroyehun, Vivian Chinelo Ugwuja, Anthony Ojonimi Onoja
pmc-11286854.description: The constant changes experienced in agricultural activities due to climate change pose a great challenge to melon production. Hence, this research examined the determinants of melon farmers’ adaptation strategies to cope with climate change hazards in southern–southern Nigeria. The research ultimately depended on primary data collected by using a set of questionnaires and interviews.

pmc-11478509.title: Adapted Low-FODMAP Diet in IBS Patients with and without Fibromyalgia: Long-Term Adherence and Outcomes
pmc-11478509.creator: Christian Lambiase, Alessandra Rossi, Riccardo Morganti, Lorenzo Cancelli, Antonio Grosso, Riccardo Tedeschi, Francesco Rettura, Marta Mosca, Nicola de Bortoli, Massimo Bellini, Jose Antonio Uranga
pmc-11478509.description: Background/Objectives: A low-FODMAPs Diet (LFD) is considered a “second line” dietary strategy for irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) but, after a period of strict restriction of all FODMAP foods, it has to be adapted and tailored to each patient (AdLFD). Fibromyalgia often coexists with IBS in up to 65% of cases.

pmc-11481530.title: Serosurveillance of Coxiella burnetii in feral swine populations of Hawaiʻi and Texas identifies overlap with human Q fever incidence
pmc-11481530.creator: Ian A. McMillan, Michael H. Norris, Samuel J. Golon, Gregory A. Franckowiak, James M. Grinolds, Samuel M. Goldstein, Darrin M. Phelps, Michael J. Bodenchuk, Bruce R. Leland, Richard A. Bowen, Vienna R. Brown, Bradley R. Borlee
pmc-11481530.description: Feral swine are invasive in the United States and a reservoir for infectious diseases. The increase in feral swine population and the geographic range are a concern for the spread of zoonotic diseases to humans and livestock. Feral swine could contribute to the spread of Coxiella burnetii, the causative agent of human Q fever.

pmc-11573936.title: A Retrospective Cohort Study to Determine Real-World Treatment Patterns in Patients with Sézary Syndrome in the United States
pmc-11573936.creator: Robert Ristuccia, Yang Zhao, Chunlan Chang, Huanxue Zhou, Takeshi Takahashi, Takanobu Nomura, Eslie Dennis, Oleg Akilov
pmc-11573936.description: IntroductionSézary syndrome (SS) is a rare leukemic cutaneous T cell lymphoma. This study was conducted to examine the real-world treatment patterns among patients with SS in the USA from 2018 to 2020.Methods This was a retrospective cohort study using the Symphony Health Solutions claims database.

pmc-13079940.title: Diffusive spreading across dynamic mitochondrial network architectures
pmc-13079940.creator: Keaton B. Holt, Camryn Zurita, Lizzy Teryoshin, Samantha C. Lewis, Elena F. Koslover
pmc-13079940.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SignificanceMitochondria form dynamic networks of interconnected tubules, with network structure varying across nutrient condition, disease state, and cell type. Numerous cellular functions rely on the sharing of ions, proteins, lipids, and RNAs throughout the mitochondrial network. In order to understand how network structure controls biomolecular distribution within mitochondria, we develop a quantitative framework for diffusive spreading on networks formed by fusion and fission.

pmc-13100046.title: Multi-scale experimental and computational assessment of heat transfer behavior in compact short fin structures
pmc-13100046.creator: Sampath Suranjan Salins, Aswathi Pallikkara Kuttiatoor, Gagan Pramod, Shiva Kumar
pmc-13100046.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The present study presents a comparative analysis of temperature distribution and heat transfer performance of short fins using experimental, simulation and theoretical method. An experimental setup was developed to investigate square, circular, rectangular, trapezoidal, and triangular fins under a constant heat input of 30 W, with specimen lengths of 0–80 mm, temperatures of 77–50 °C, and natural convection conditions (ambient air at 25 °C, velocity 0.2 to 0.5 m/s).

pmc-13254572.title: Meropenem stress drives lipid remodeling and resistance gene dissemination via outer membrane vesicles in carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae
pmc-13254572.creator: Fangfang Fan, Qiuyuan Shi, Guangzhang Chen, Huahan Zhan, Siqian Deng, Yibing Peng, Li Wei
pmc-13254572.description: Highlights•CRKP-derived outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) serve as multifunctional vectors for antibiotic resistance, encapsulating a diverse array of lipids and harboring the carbapenemase gene blaKPC-2.•Meropenem stress triggers a marked upregulation of membrane lipids in CRKP-OMVs, particularly sphingolipids (SP), glycerolipids (GL), glycerophospholipids (GP), and fatty acids (FA), which likely fortify bacterial antibiotic resistance through enhanced membrane stability and efflux efficiency.

pmc-13477281.title: Efficacy and Safety of Pharmaceutically Manufactured Cannabidiol in Recurrent Pericarditis: A Phase II Clinical Trial
pmc-13477281.creator: Sushil Allen Luis, Allan L Klein, Paul C Cremer, Antonio Abbate, Jonathan R Salik, Georgia K Thomas, Syed Waqas Haider, Tracy E Hagerty, David Lin, Thomas E Waggoner, Stephen J Nicholls, Bridget‐Anne Kirwan, Kelly A D Narine, Andrea B Parker, Andrew Hamer
pmc-13477281.description: BackgroundRecurrent pericarditis may be mediated through inappropriate activation of the NACHT, leucine‐rich repeat, and pyrin domain‐containing protein 3 inflammasome. Pharmaceutically manufactured cannabidiol is an oral formulation that inhibits NACHT, leucine‐rich repeat, and pyrin domain‐containing protein 3 inflammasome activation and development of pericarditis in a preclinical model.
